ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Low ratio; dominant low-intensity (black/dark-grey) pixels account for over 90% of the visible surface, with high-intensity (white) pixels localized to discrete scarring and distal clusters.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous black/dark-grey field. High-contrast white ring-like formations (rosettes) are distributed sporadically across both lobes. Dense, multi-tonal (white/tan) contiguous geometric clusters are located at the extreme distal tips of both the left and right lobes.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central notch with an estimated interior angle of approximately 68 degrees and a well-defined vertex point.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations along the entire trailing edge boundary. Significant jagged peaks and valleys ranging from 5 to 30 pixels in amplitude, particularly prominent on the outer thirds of both lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex sweep trajectory originating from the central notch, arching upwards and outwards toward the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Multiple circular and semi-circular white high-contrast rings (5-20 pixel diameters) detected; high-density clusters are visible in the mid-left lobe and central-right lobe sections.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Single vertical linear pixel disruption of light pigment (approx. 120 pixels in length) detected on the lateral portion of the right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive calcified barnacle colonization (Coronula diadema) at both distal tips, creating raised, textured masses. Significant white circular scarring (rosettes) from previous parasitic attachment across the ventral surface.
other_distinctive_markers: The distal tips exhibit a highly irregular, 'cauliflower' silhouette due to the density of the protruding barnacle clusters.
